title: The Last Train
introduction: Do you enjoy a good scare? Read the short story below.

sentences: Ron Green was taking the last train home from Bonnington to Chisley.
The rain began hitting the carriage window as he checked his watch: 23.45.
paragraphs.zh: 羅恩・格林乘搭尾班火車，從邦寧頓返回奇斯利的家。他看錶時，雨點開始打在車廂窗上：23時45分。

sentences: ‘Still ages to go,’ he muttered grumpily.
‘Can't we go a bit faster?’
paragraphs.zh: 「還要很久才到。」他不耐煩地嘟囔。「就不能開快一點嗎？」

sentences: The only other soul in the carriage was a man several rows ahead, facing away from him.
The man was wearing a black baseball cap and red sweatshirt.
Despite his very ordinary choice of outfit, something about the man gave Ron a sense of déjà vu.
paragraphs.zh: 車廂裏除了他，就只有幾排座位前一名背對着他的男子。那人戴着黑色棒球帽，穿着紅色衛衣。衣着雖然平凡，羅恩卻總覺得他似曾相識。

sentences: ‘Excuse me?’ Ron called over.
‘Do I know you?’
paragraphs.zh: 「不好意思？」羅恩朝他喊道。「我們認識嗎？」

sentences: The man did not move.
‘Must be asleep,’ Ron told himself.
Soon after, the gentle rocking of the train lulled him, too, into sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 那人一動也不動。「大概睡着了。」羅恩心想。不久，火車輕輕搖晃，也把他哄睡了。

sentences: The train jolted and Ron's eyes sprang open.
The man appeared to be a little closer now.
paragraphs.zh: 火車猛然一晃，羅恩驟然睜眼。那名男子似乎靠近了一點。

sentences: ‘Perhaps his seat was uncomfortable,’ Ron thought, and fell back to sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 「也許他原來的座位不舒服。」羅恩心想，然後又睡了過去。

sentences: Five minutes later, he awoke once more.
The man was now just one row away.
paragraphs.zh: 五分鐘後，他再次醒來。那名男子如今只隔着一排座位。

sentences: ‘Perhaps his armrest was broken,’ Ron speculated, as he started to feel a little uneasy.
paragraphs.zh: 「也許他的扶手壞了。」羅恩猜想，卻開始有點不安。

sentences: Again, Ron allowed himself to drift off.
Shortly after, he awoke to the sound of his watch beeping.
It was midnight.
There was no sign of the man.
He turned and let out a small scream.
In the seat beside him sat the man, staring directly at him.
Ron stared back and could hardly believe what he saw.
It was like looking into a mirror, except that the man's face was dripping with blood.
paragraphs.zh: 羅恩又迷迷糊糊睡着了。不久，手錶的嗶嗶聲把他吵醒。午夜到了。那名男子不見蹤影。他轉過頭，低聲驚叫。男子就坐在他旁邊，直直盯着他。羅恩回望，幾乎不敢相信自己的眼睛。對方簡直是鏡中的自己，只是臉上淌着血。

sentences: ‘Has my demise taught you nothing?’ said the man with great tenderness.
‘More haste, less speed.
Remember?
Rush your life away and it will quickly disappear.’
paragraphs.zh: 「我的死還沒有讓你學到教訓嗎？」那人溫柔地說。「欲速則不達。記得嗎？一味匆忙度日，生命也會很快消逝。」

sentences: Ron's doppelganger then closed his eyes and slumped forward in his seat.
Nearly petrified, Ron edged past the corpse and ran like the wind through carriage after carriage.
Eventually, he slumped down into a seat, breathing hard.
Yesterday's newspaper lay on the table before him.
The headline read, ‘Remembering the Victims on the Anniversary of the Bonnington Train Crash.’
paragraphs.zh: 羅恩的分身隨即閉上眼，向前癱倒在座位上。羅恩嚇得幾乎動彈不得，小心繞過屍體，飛奔穿過一節又一節車廂。最後，他跌坐在座位上，氣喘吁吁。面前的桌上放着昨天的報紙。標題寫着：「邦寧頓火車意外周年：悼念罹難者。」

sentences: Ron read on, ‘The only survivor of the crash, caused by a speeding train, was Ron Green.
He has sustained grave brain injuries and is still in a coma.
His identical twin, Martin, sadly did not survive the crash.’
paragraphs.zh: 羅恩繼續讀下去：「這宗因列車超速而造成的意外，唯一生還者是羅恩・格林。他腦部受重創，至今仍然昏迷。他的同卵雙胞胎兄弟馬丁則不幸罹難。」

sentences: The train sped on, faster and faster.
paragraphs.zh: 火車繼續疾駛，愈來愈快。
